title: LLM latency + economics reading sprint — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump from a few papers/blogs and ideas for experiments to reduce tail latency and token cost. Not polished — a sprint scratchpad.

Top-level takeaways (short):
- Tail latency matters a lot for UX and for cost (timeouts, retries, wasted tokens). We should think in percentiles rather than averages when suggesting defaults to customers.
- Small config changes (prefetch KV, early exit heuristics, slightly larger batching) can shift p99 normally without much cost. Need controlled A/B.
- Quantization saves dollars but can introduce soft regressions on rare long-context continuations — create regression probes focused on long-tailed prompts.

Papers/blogs skimmed (quick notes):
1) "Practical tail-latency reduction in RPC systems" (industry blog summary) — lessons: staggered retry windows, head-of-line blocking avoidance, and circuit breaker thresholds tied to GPU queue depth. Relevance: map GPU queue depth -> per-route fallback to lower-capacity model before queue crosses threshold.
2) "Adaptive batching for transformers" (arXiv 2025-ish) — continuous batching with latency SLO constraint. Key idea: maintain queue, release batches at dynamic size to meet SLO. Implementation notes: we already have batching hooks; add a scheduling policy that uses the median sequence length and current load.
3) "KV cache eviction policies for long-context workloads" — comparison of LRU, size-aware, and semantic-importance eviction. Finding: semantic-aware (drop tokens with low attention mass) works best but is expensive. Practical: hybrid LRU + sample-based importance scoring (cheap approximation).
4) "Quantization and hallucination tradeoffs" — small quantization (8-bit) OK for short prompts; 4-bit aggressive quant can degrade factual continuations on certain tokens (dates, numbers). Need a focused evaluation suite.

Concrete experiment list (prioritized):
- E1 (quick): Add a p95/p99 monitor for GPU queue depth per model route (store 60d). Alert when p99 queue length > X. Tag correlated customer routes. (ticket: JIRA-1142)
- E2: Canary adaptive-batching scheduler on one low-volume model (ms-13b) with SLO=200ms. Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-second. Compare cost/unit.
- E3: Build a small long-context probe set (50 prompts) that stresses numerical continuity and rare token fidelity. Run against float32, int8, and 4-bit quant. Record exact-match rates at token-level and high-level semantic errors.
- E4: KV eviction prototype: sample-based importance scoring every N steps (cheap dot-product-based) + LRU fallback. Measure cache hitrate and avg seq len served.
- E5: Fallback routing policy: when queue depth or GPU TTF (time-to-free) predicts p99 > threshold, route to model-variant with lower mem/cost (quantized or fewer layers) with auto-retry/backoff. Watch for quality regressions.

Observability / metrics I want:
- Per-request: model-id, sequence-length, kv-hit (bool), batching-delay-ms, queue-depth-at-arrival, tokens-emitted, final-latency-ms, fallback-used (bool), quant-profile.
- Aggregates: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency by route/model variant; cost-per-token and tokens-per-dollar by percentile; quality-regression-rate computed from eval probes.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How noisy is queue-depth signal across hosts? Do we need host-level smoothing or cross-host rolling windows?
- How much offline eval coverage is enough to catch quant-induced regressions before customer impact? Thresholds?
- What's the right SLI definition for "acceptable degradation" when routing to cheaper variant? (5% semantic error? 3% perplexity change?)

Quick action items (next 2 weeks):
- Wire up queue-depth metric to tracing spans (Evan) -> add histogram to Console (Samir).
- Draft long-context probe prompt list (me): include 10 numeric continuity, 10 instruction-following long completion, 10 code continuation, 10 dialog with entity persistence, 10 nested reasoning steps. Put in repo: runtime/evals/long_context_probe.json.
- Spin up canary for adaptive batching on staging GPU pool. Collect 48h stable traffic trace.

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Remember to include tokenization alignment checks in quant evals (tokenizer differences can look like hallucination).
- Consider a "graceful degrade" template for customers: pre-signup info about expected delta when switching to quantized fallback.
- Add a small synthetic workload that triggers long-tail (many short then sudden long sequences) to simulate chat apps that escalate.

References / links I want to follow up:
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.XXXX (adaptive batching paper)
- https://engineering.example.com/blog/kv-cache-evictions
- https://github.com/quant-repo/benchmarks (for quant comparison scripts)

Bottom line: low-hanging wins are observability + canary adaptive-batching + small targeted probe sets for quant regressions. More ambitious: semantic-aware KV eviction but budget time.

TODO markers: 
- [ ] create long_context_probe.json (path above)
- [ ] make JIRA tickets for E2/E3/E4 if not present
- [ ] add docs entry in Confluence: /INF/latency-econ-playbook (link above)

Random quick brainstorm (one-liners):
- Could we pre-warm KV cache for premium customers with predicted next-token distributions? (expensive but maybe for very high-value flows)
- Token-aware batching: prioritize requests that share prefixes to boost cache reuse inside same batch.

End of sprint scratchpad. Will convert high-value bits into PRD if experiments return promising signal.
